{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the belly line (stroke 2), the long lower curve of the fish body, from the nose across to the tail stem. This is one of the two main outline strokes that give the judge the body shape. I laid it in sustained runs of ten dominoes, and it was across by the three-minute mark. Hana's lower tail fork was set to lay itself once the belly reached the tail, so getting it across early let the tail work proceed.

Execution: I inspected the nose join several times to find where the fall was breaking, and I closed gaps with short bridging runs and re-stood dominoes where needed. In the final minutes I put in a join from the end of the start row into the belly line, with a gentle curve to fit the table's fall rules. I kept my hands off the area once it was set so nothing would be bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I backed Hana's suggestion to start at the nose, and I held off building until the new sketch was up so no work was wasted. I stayed clear of the nose while Jack was rebuilding it. I split the joins with Hana, with her on the top bridge and me on the belly, and I called out my moves so we didn't nudge the same dominoes.

Leadership: I kept the table coordinated. I made sure the start stroke was laid first so the fall would split at the nose. I proposed dry runs once the lines were across, and I set clear hands-off rules around the join so our fixes didn't undo each other. I called out the time pressure as the minutes ran down so the table stayed focused on getting the fish to fall.", "my_share_percent": 30}
